items.q: What is the West's biggest misunderstanding about China's economy?
items.a: "The biggest misunderstanding is somehow that a group of people, or even just one person, **runs the entire Chinese economy**." Beneath political centralization sits the **mayor economy** — local prefects competing on GDP (and shifting yardsticks like environment). Keyu says it's "more **decentralized** than the US's."

items.q: Why did Deng-era reforms work when Soviet planning failed?
items.a: Local officials were **incentivized to experiment** (SEZs, surplus retention, WTO 2001): success rolled out nationally, failure stayed contained — "cat black or white" pragmatism, not one leader's decree or a Soviet ministry model.

items.q: Is China communist or capitalist in practice?
items.a: Economically **hyper-capitalist** (ferocious competition, replication over differentiation); socially **socialist-communal** (SOEs, state banks, common prosperity rhetoric). Private firms aren't uniformly suppressed — local governments help promising ones (**DeepSeek is private**).

items.q: What is the "tallest tree" rule for Chinese founders?
items.a: "The tallest tree gets the **most wind**." Jack Ma / Ant Group lesson: don't be colorful politically; **capital stays subordinate to politics**. Pros: speed and market feedback. Cons: weak bankruptcy/IP and "evil competitors."

items.q: How does China innovate differently from the US or Europe?
items.a: **Innovate first, regulate after** (vs Europe's regulate-first). US leads **zero-to-one** breakthroughs; China leads **diffusion**, scale, and cost-cutting (DeepSeek, Xiaomi EVs).

items.q: Did US chip sanctions slow China down?
items.a: Keyu argues they **backfired** as crisis innovation: Huawei/DeepSeek domestic capacity accelerated under a "whole-of-nation" Olympic-gold mentality. "When the Chinese were comfortably importing chips… the whole industry **stalled for 20 years**." Comfort breeds complacency.

items.q: How does China approach Trump-era tariffs?
items.a: Principles: **equivalence, reciprocity, realism**. Red lines on mixing Hong Kong/Taiwan with trade; **face-saving** is essential. Tariffs hurt US, China, and the intermediate-goods chain — better to strengthen domestic competitiveness (1980s US-Japan semiconductor analogy).

items.q: What would a realistic US-China deal look like?
items.a: **US goods purchases + market access + IP protection** — not forcing political model change. China prepared ~**5 years** for tariff rounds with calibrated assertiveness.

items.q: How did the one-child policy reshape the economy?
items.a: It drove **high savings**, six-wallet housing, inverted family hierarchy, and gender education gains — but fertility is now **too low**. Aging is less catastrophic than **skill-gap mismatch**; post-1990 aging societies got richer via automation.

items.q: Why do "China collapse" predictions keep failing?
items.a: "**Collapse** is such a strong word" — repeated ~**4–6 times** since the 1980s during the fastest growth. Expect **slowdown**, not collapse. Bottleneck: the **consumption gap**. Advice: "Go dig deep and don't just go to **Beijing and Shanghai**."
